body:
I do not reproduce the compilation error with/without strict option.
I think this is expected because:
1. formState is declared of type **O**bject. (so we can assing value to it, but invoke only the methods defined in the Object interface )
1. If it were declared of type **o**bject (the type used to describe non-primitive types), then passing a string(primitive value in TypeScript) would have resulted in the error mentioned above
@rafaelss95 am I missing something here ? A simple repo otherwise that I can clone to reproduce would be great.

Anyway, I agree that to be coherent with FormControl constructor, FormBuilder#control method should have the formState parameter of type any instead of Object.

I would like to provide a pull request for that

@benbraou You're totally right. The error that I mentioned happens when you try to initialize a `control` with `null` or `undefined` (of course with `--strict` option enabled).

Examples:

```
this.formBuilder.control(null); // Argument of type 'null' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Object'.
this.formBuilder.control(undefined); // Argument of type 'undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Object'.
```
Hi, out of curiosity - how would one go about writing a test for such thing? I mean testing that something works specifically with the `--strict` option enabled

issue.title: fix(forms): allow FormBuilder to create controls with any formState type
